title: The Whip's Crack: A Sound Barrier Broken by Hand
summary: A translation of the same day's science episode. A whip's crack is a small sonic boom: a flick of the wrist sends a loop running along the tapering whip, and the tip ends up moving faster than sound. The episode follows how this was worked out, from early twentieth-century shadow photographs that caught the shock wave to modern models of how the loop speeds up as the whip narrows, and why the exact source of the crack is still debated.
